text: I:\C_L\CL.51 15.docx E 4 ALBERT EMBANKMENT LONDON SE1 7SR Telephone: +44 (0)20 7735 7611 Circular Letter No. 5115 30 January 2026 To: All IMO Member States Subject: Call for expression s of interest (EOIs): Future -Ready Shipping (FRS) in Africa project support for enhancement of maritime single window (MSW) readiness and data-driven , digitalized maritime oversight in Sub-Saharan Africa Overview of Future -Ready Shipping (FRS) in Africa 1 Efficient maritime trade and transport facilitation are essential to the smooth functioning of global supply chains and the competitiveness of national ports. The IMO Facilitation (FAL) Convention establishes a framework for the simplification, standardiza tion and harmonization of maritime transport formalities, including the mandatory implementation of a Maritime Single Window (MSW) to enable the electronic exchange of information required for ship arrival, stay and departure. a Maritime Single Window (MSW) to enable the electronic exchange of information required for ship arrival, stay and departure. Effective MSW implementation plays a critical role in reducing administrative burdens, improving port efficiency, enhancing regulatory compliance, strengthening maritime oversight, and enabling secure, data -driven decision -making across public and private stakeholders. 2 In addition to trade facilitation benefits, MSW implementation provides a foundation for enhanced maritime oversight, improved data quality, and the integration of digital systems supporting vessel monitoring, risk assessment, and environmental reporting. The FRS in Africa project is designed to support the African continent 's transition toward s a sustainable, decarbonized and digitally advanced maritime sector, while strengthening institutional capacity, regional cooperation and investment readiness. The FRS in Africa project is implemented by the International Maritime Organization (IMO)

The FRS in Africa project is implemented by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and funded by the European Union (EU). 3 Recognizing the specific needs and opportunities of Sub -Saharan African Member States , IMO invites expressions of interest (EOIs) from eligible Member States to participate in targeted technical assistance activities aimed at comprehensive MSW readiness assessments identifying interoperability gaps, data security risks, legal and regulatory shortcomings, technical limitations, and change management challenges. 4 The Facilitation Committee, at its forty -ninth session (10 to 14 March 2025), approved the Guidelines for setting up a Maritime Single Window (FAL.5/Circ.42/Rev.4 ). ow (FAL.5/Circ.42/Rev.4 ). The selected beneficiary Member States will receive technical assistance under the project to support readiness assessments and the development of draft MSW road maps with timelines, resource needs, and technical specifications, while ensuring alignment with IMO instruments, safety considerations, and national priorities. Circular Letter No. 5115 Page 2 I:\C_L\CL.5115.docx Assistance provided by the FRS in Africa project 5 The Future -Ready Shipping (FRS) in Africa project will provide support in: • Assessment of digital readiness and infrastructure gaps for implementing a Maritime Single Window (MSW); • Mapping existing port community systems (PCS), MSW -related platforms, and IT infrastructure, including: o identification of interoperability gaps; o data security and cyber risk considerations; o legal and regulatory shortcomings; o technical limitations; and o change management and institutional challenges; • Conducting situational analyses of national poli

ty and cyber risk considerations; o legal and regulatory shortcomings; o technical limitations; and o change management and institutional challenges; • Conducting situational analyses of national policy, legal and regulatory frameworks relevant to MSW implementation and maritime digitalization; • Assessing the feasibility of adapting or integrating electronic ship and vessel registry systems to support maritime oversight, including GHG emissions data collection and reporting; • Developing draft MSW road maps , including: o phased implementation timelines; o institutional roles and responsibilities; o resource and capacity requirements; and o high-level technical and interoperability specifications; and • Organizing multi -stakeholder workshops to validate assessment findings and proposed road maps with public and private sector stakeholders. 6 Please note that the assistance provided does not include any form of direct cash or financial assistance.
